newsitem.title: UK: Sewage-loving gulls could spread E coli - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Sewage-loving gulls could spread E coli - magazine.

text.p: Seagulls feasting on sewage, garbage dumps and farm waste could help to spread the poisonous E coli bacteria, New Scientist magazine said on Thursday.

Researchers for Britain's Public Health Laboratory Service and the University of Lancaster analysed 700 samples of gull droppings and found three percent were infected with E coli 0157, a strain of a common gut bacteria that can cause food poisoning.
The birds roost on farmland and defecate onto grass and into cattle troughs, which could spread the bacteria to cattle.
"If it's out in the environment in the birds, it is likely to spread from farm to farm," Keith Jones of the University of Lancaster told New Scientist.
An E coli outbreak killed 19 elderly people in Scotland late last year and early this year. The bacteria can cause brain and kidney damage in the vulnerable, such as young children and the elderly.
It can be spread to meat through improper slaughterhouse hygiene or onto fruit and vegetables fertilised with manure.
